library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2019_dexmedetomidine"))$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2019.00756>
* Trial registration: NCT03337581

Dexmedetomidine is a selective alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonist used for
perioperative and procedural sedation. Wang 2019 gave a single 1 ug/kg
intranasal dose (undiluted 100 ug/mL solution, applied as drops from a 1-mL
syringe) to 13 Chinese children under general anaesthesia, 30 min before the
end of surgery, and sampled arterial plasma for 180 min. A two-compartment
model with first-order absorption and fixed allometric weight scaling
standardised to 70 kg described the data. The article has no supplementary
material, and no erratum was found (EuropePMC title search, 2026-11-25).

# Population

Wang 2019 Table 1 (n = 13; 145 arterial samples):

| Characteristic | Value |
|---|---|
| Sex (female / male) | 8 / 5 |
| Age (years) | 6.5 +/- 1.7 (4-10) |
| Weight (kg) | 24.8 +/- 5.8 (14-36) |
| Height (cm) | 110 +/- 12 (83-130) |
| Serum creatinine (umol/L) | 37.3 +/- 7.3 (23.8-47.0) |
| Creatinine clearance (mL/min) | 99.2 +/- 19.0 (78.2-150) |

Children were scheduled for orthopaedic, lower abdominal, urologic or plastic
surgery (expected duration at least 2 h), with propofol/fentanyl induction and
sevoflurane maintenance. All samples were above the 0.01 ng/mL limit of
quantitation. The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Wang_2019_dexmedetomidine")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Element | Value in the model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | 2-compartment, first-order absorption, no lag | Results: 2-cmt OFV 1331.0 vs 1-cmt 1344.6; lag time did not improve the fit (OFV 1330.5) |
| `lka` | log(0.0378) 1/min | Table 2 'Ka (1/min)' |
| `lcl` | log(0.319) L/min per 70 kg | Table 2 'CL/F (L/min/70 kg)' |
| `lvc` | log(34.2) L per 70 kg | Table 2 'V1/F (L/70 kg)' |
| `lq` | log(10.0) L/min per 70 kg | Table 2 'Q2/F (L/min/70 kg)' |
| `lvp` | log(34.9) L per 70 kg | Table 2 'V2/F (L/70 kg)' |
| `e_wt_cl_q`, `e_wt_vc_vp` | fixed 0.75, fixed 1 | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic Modeling' power model `(BW/70)^PBW`; Results: 'exponent of 1 for all volumes and of 0.75 for all clearances' |
| `etalka`, `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalq` | 0.0112, 0.0207, 0.00569, 1.29 | Table 2 'Interindividual variability omega2' (variances of exponential etas, Methods `Pi = PTV * exp(eta_i)`) |
| IIV on V2/F | none | Table 2 '0 (fixed)'; Results: variance < 0.0001, fixed to zero |
| `addSd` | sqrt(1752) = 41.857 pg/mL | Table 2 'sigma2 add' = 1752; proportional term removed (Results: sigma2 prop < 0.0001) |
| `Cc` | `central / vc * 1000` | dose in ug, volume in L, concentrations reported in pg/mL |

# Typical-value replication of Table 3

Table 3 of the paper lists the typical-value pharmacokinetics for children of
10, 20, 30 and 40 kg after 1 ug/kg intranasally. These are deterministic model
outputs, so the packaged model must reproduce them to the printed precision.
The half-lives are the eigenvalues of the two-compartment system and Tpeak /
Cpeak come from a dense typical-value solve.

```{r table3}
mod <- readModelDb("Wang_2019_dexmedetomidine")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

wts <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
ev_typ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(wts), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    id = i, WT = wts[i],
    time = c(0, seq(0, 300, by = 0.01)),
    amt = c(wts[i], rep(0, 30001)),
    evid = c(1, rep(0, 30001)),
    cmt = c("depot", rep("central", 30001))
  )
}))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
                           returnType = "data.frame", keep = "WT")

eig <- function(w) {
  cl <- 0.319 * (w / 70)^0.75; q <- 10.0 * (w / 70)^0.75
  v1 <- 34.2 * w / 70; v2 <- 34.9 * w / 70
  k10 <- cl / v1; k12 <- q / v1; k21 <- q / v2
  a <- k10 + k12 + k21; b <- sqrt(a^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)
  c(CL = cl, V1 = v1, Vss = v1 + v2,
    thalf_a = log(2) / ((a + b) / 2), thalf_b = log(2) / ((a - b) / 2))
}

ours <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(WT) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Tpeak = time[which.max(Cc)], Cpeak = max(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::bind_cols(as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, lapply(wts, eig))))

published_t3 <- data.frame(
  WT = wts,
  CL = c(0.0740, 0.124, 0.169, 0.209),
  V1 = c(4.88, 9.76, 14.6, 19.5),
  Vss = c(9.87, 19.7, 29.6, 39.5),
  thalf_a = c(0.73, 0.87, 0.96, 1.03),
  thalf_b = c(93.1, 111, 123, 132),
  Tpeak = c(52.4, 55.6, 57.5, 58.9),
  Cpeak = c(675, 704, 720, 731)
)

cmp_t3 <- tidyr::pivot_longer(published_t3, -WT, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "published") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(ours, -WT, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "packaged"),
    by = c("WT", "quantity")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (packaged / published - 1))

cmp_t3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(packaged = signif(packaged, 4), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 2)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Weight (kg)" = WT, "Quantity" = quantity, "Wang 2019 Table 3" = published,
    "Packaged model" = packaged, "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Wang 2019 (typical child, 1 ug/kg intranasal).")

# Every Table 3 entry is printed to 3 significant figures (2 for the
# shortest half-lives), so the packaged model must agree within rounding.
# A mis-transcribed parameter, exponent, reference weight or unit factor
# moves at least one row by several percent.
stopifnot(max(abs(cmp_t3$pct_diff)) < 0.8)
```

All 32 entries agree within the rounding of the printed table, which
confirms the parameter values, the 70 kg standardisation, the allometric
exponents, the absence of a weight effect on Ka and the pg/mL unit factor at
once.

# Virtual cohort

Body weights are drawn from a normal distribution with the Table 1 mean and SD
(24.8 +/- 5.8 kg), restricted to the observed 14-36 kg range by rejection and
redraw, so the cohort keeps the published spread instead of piling up at the
bounds. The dose is 1 ug/kg and the observation grid is the paper's arterial
sampling schedule, extended to 12 h so that a terminal half-life can be
estimated.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190705)
n_sub <- 200
draw_wt <- function(n) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- stats::rnorm(2 * n, 24.8, 5.8)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= 14 & x <= 36])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}
wt <- draw_wt(n_sub)

obs_times <- c(0, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180,
               240, 300, 360, 480, 600, 720)
ev <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    id = i, WT = wt[i],
    time = c(0, obs_times),
    amt = c(wt[i], rep(0, length(obs_times))),
    evid = c(1, rep(0, length(obs_times))),
    cmt = c("depot", rep("central", length(obs_times)))
  )
}))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190705)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "WT")
```

# Concentration-time profiles

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Simulated individual profiles over the 180-min sampling window (compare Figure 1 of Wang 2019, which shows the 13 measured profiles)."}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 180, id <= 30) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, sim, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "Time after intranasal dose (min)", y = "Dexmedetomidine (pg/mL)",
       title = "30 simulated children, 1 ug/kg intranasal (with residual error)")
```

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles (compare the prediction-corrected VPC in Figure 3 of Wang 2019; observed Cmax 713-795 pg/mL)."}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 180) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(713, 795), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Time after intranasal dose (min)", y = "Dexmedetomidine (pg/mL)")
```

# NCA with PKNCA

Peak metrics are taken over the paper's 0-180 min sampling schedule; the
terminal half-life is estimated over the extended grid. NCA uses the
individual predictions `Cc` (no residual error).

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "1 ug/kg IN") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose <- ev |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "1 ug/kg IN") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0), end = c(180, Inf),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)
```

Wang 2019 reports arithmetic means (observed Cmax and Tmax from Results; the
terminal half-life from the individual Bayesian estimates), so the simulated
values are aggregated as means before comparison.

```{r nca_compare}
sim_mean <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

published_nca <- data.frame(
  treatment = "1 ug/kg IN",
  cmax = 748,      # Results: maximum measured concentration 748 +/- 29.6 pg/mL
  tmax = 49.6,     # Results: observed time to maximum 49.6 +/- 7.21 min
  half.life = 117  # Results: terminal elimination half-life 117 +/- 16.1 min
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_mean,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "pg/mL", tmax = "min", half.life = "min"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published mean NCA (1 ug/kg intranasal). * differs from reference by >20%.")

cmax_ratio <- sim_mean$PPORRES[sim_mean$PPTESTCD == "cmax"] / 748
thalf_ratio <- sim_mean$PPORRES[sim_mean$PPTESTCD == "half.life"] / 117
# Centre-of-distribution checks only; a dose, unit or clearance error moves
# these by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(cmax_ratio - 1) < 0.15, abs(thalf_ratio - 1) < 0.20)
```

Observed Tmax is read on the 45/60 min sampling points, so it is coarser than
the model's continuous Tpeak (the paper's own simulated Tpeak was 55.2 +/- 5.96
min). The observed Cmax spread (SD 29.6 pg/mL, range 713-795) is much
narrower than the cohort above, because the model also carries the
between-subject variability of Ka, CL/F and V1/F and residual error.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No bioavailability.** No intravenous arm was studied; all disposition
  parameters are apparent (divided by F) and the model applies no `f(depot)`.
  Doses enter `depot` at the nominal amount.
* **IIV on V2/F omitted.** Table 2 reports the V2/F variance as 0 (fixed); the
  model carries no eta on `lvp`, which is equivalent.
* **Large IIV on Q2/F.** The Q2/F variance of 1.29 (about 113% CV on the
  log scale) is reproduced as published. The authors note it is the least
  well-estimated parameter (highest shrinkage and RSE).
* **Residual error.** Additive only, SD = sqrt(1752) = 41.9 pg/mL, as printed.
* **Haemodynamics not modelled.** Figure 4 (MAP and heart rate) is
  descriptive; the paper fits no PD model, so none is packaged.
* **Virtual cohort.** Weights are drawn from a normal distribution with the
  Table 1 mean and SD restricted to the observed range; age, sex and renal
  function were screened and not retained, so they are not simulated.
